sections.h2: Who is selling a house in Miami, and who is buying?
sections.html:
Mostly owners in a city of renters. The Census Bureau estimates 489,812 residents in July 2025 across 36.00 square miles of land, up 10.8 percent from the 2020 estimates base, and counts only 30.8 percent of 194,821 households as owner-occupied for 2020 through 2024.

The same page shows 57.7 percent of residents born abroad and 77.2 percent of those five and older speaking another language at home. A seller should expect bilingual showings and should have a contract translated or explained before anyone signs.

sections.h2: Can a Miami owner keep the house and rent it by the night?
sections.html:
Rarely. The city's short-term rental page says houses and duplexes in T3 and T4-R transect zones are generally not eligible for short-term rental or lodging use, and it ties that position to City of Miami v. Airbnb.

Conversions of apartments and condos face a longer checklist: a Certificate of Occupancy, a state lodging license, a Certificate of Use, a Business Tax Receipt and any county approvals. The Certificate of Use renews yearly and the city may audit or inspect without notice. Once more than 25 percent of a building's units operate as short-term rentals, the building is treated as transient, which brings an occupancy reclassification and added code work.

Check zoning with the city before you count on nightly income as an alternative to selling.

sections.h2: Does Miami-Dade's recertification rule apply to my property?
sections.html:
Not to a single family house. The county's recertification page says single-family homes, duplexes, and buildings with an occupant load of ten or less and 2,000 square feet or less do not go through the process. It matters mostly to condo and apartment owners.

For buildings that are covered, the county says the program began in 1975 and was amended June 1, 2022 after a state law on milestone inspections of condominium and cooperative buildings of three stories or more. Coastal condo buildings of that height within three miles of the shoreline built on or after 1998 are inspected at 25 years, other newer buildings at 30, and each repeats every ten years.

  • The owner receives a Notice of Required Recertification.
  • A written report from a Florida-registered engineer or architect is due within 90 days of the notice.
  • The report certifies the structure is structurally and electrically safe for continued occupancy.

A condo seller should have the building's recertification status in the document package.

sections.h2: How are Miami-Dade deed taxes different?
sections.html:
Miami-Dade is the one county with its own formula. The state revenue department prints 60 cents per hundred dollars plus a 45 cent surtax, with the surtax skipped on a document that transfers only a single-family dwelling. Every other county charges 70 cents.

The base counts any mortgage that stays on the property, so a payoff does not shrink it. All parties on the instrument are liable regardless of who the contract names, which is why that clause deserves a slow read.

  • Clerk recording charges under section 28.24 of the Florida Statutes.
  • Payoffs for mortgages, judgments and unpaid taxes.
  • A draft settlement statement you review before signing.

sections.h2: What does Miami-Dade's tax calendar mean at closing?
sections.html:
Two county offices share the work: the Property Appraiser assesses and the Tax Collector bills. The appraiser says it does not mail bills or collect, so balance questions go to the collector.

The appraiser's public notice reports that the 2026 roll was certified October 16, 2026, and that the June 1 estimate of countywide taxable value was $540.7 billion, up 5.5 percent over 2025. A value challenge must reach the clerk within 25 days of the proposed tax notice and goes to the value adjustment board.

After a homestead sale, the next owner is assessed at full value starting the following January 1. A seller who buys again in Florida can request portability with the new homestead filing, due March 1.

sections.h2: What if the Miami house has liens, open permits or tenants?
sections.html:
A cash sale can still close if each issue is cleared or priced in. A title search surfaces mortgages, judgments and unpaid tax, and a bill still open after April 1 is delinquent with certificates sold by June 1.

Older buildings often hide open or missing permits. Ask the city's building department what is open on your parcel, then ask the buyer whether the offer takes the work as is.

  • Inherited house: the estate may need a court order before anyone can convey title, and summary administration exists for smaller estates.
  • Past-due mortgage: ask the lender for the payoff and case status in writing.
  • Tenant in place: three days' written demand for unpaid rent, weekends and court holidays excluded, or 30 days' notice to end a monthly tenancy.

sections.h2: What happens after the Miami deed is signed?
sections.html:
The clerk of court records it and takes the stamp tax while the title company clears liens. Quitclaim, warranty, special warranty and trustee's deeds are all taxable in the state's list, so changing the form does not change the result.

The appraiser's site also promotes a free clerk alert that notifies you within a day when a document is recorded against your property. Sign up before and after a sale to see what gets filed, and keep the settlement statement with your tax records.

sections.h2: What can the Miami-Dade appraiser's office do for an owner?
sections.html:
It runs two public branches, downtown and in Cutler Bay, with appointments online, plus neighborhood outreach events where staff review values, exemptions and portability one on one.

Widow, widower and disability exemptions for veterans or surviving spouses can be filed online with uploaded documents, and agricultural classification applications are online too. Staff also take reports of suspected homestead exemption fraud. Before pricing, look up your parcel's exemptions and assessed value and bring the printout to any offer discussion.

sections.h2: How should I judge a Miami cash offer?
sections.html:
Compare it with what a listing would net after fees, repairs and months of carrying costs. In the contract, find who pays the stamp tax, title policy and recording, and what happens to the deposit.

Get the closing date and closing agent in writing, and do not sign the deed until the contract is final. Pay no fee just to receive an offer. If you are unsure, request a second offer and compare terms line by line.

faqs.q: Is Miami's deed tax higher than elsewhere in Florida?
faqs.a: Its formula differs: 60 cents per hundred dollars plus a 45 cent surtax, but the surtax does not apply when only a single-family dwelling is transferred. Other counties charge 70 cents.

faqs.q: Can a Miami single-family house be a short-term rental?
faqs.a: Generally not in T3 and T4-R zones, per the city's page. Confirm your zoning with the city before planning on it.

faqs.q: Does recertification apply to a Miami single-family home?
faqs.a: No. The county exempts single-family homes, duplexes and small buildings of 2,000 square feet or less with ten or fewer occupants.

faqs.q: Who sends my Miami property tax bill?
faqs.a: The Miami-Dade Tax Collector. The Property Appraiser sets value and exemptions but does not mail bills.

faqs.q: Does my reduced assessment pass to the buyer?
faqs.a: No. A sale resets the assessment to full value the next January 1, and your savings follow you only through portability.
